title: MoC: A Morton-Code-Based Fine-Grained Quantization for Accelerating Point Cloud Neural Networks
problem: Point Cloud Neural Networks with large-scale unordered points and lengthy features require heavy computational workloads incompatible with real-time processing. This severely limits deployment in time-sensitive and safety-critical 3D applications.
motivation: Point cloud processing is critical for real-time 3D applications including autonomous systems and robotics, but current PCNNs are computationally prohibitive.
method: MoC groups nearby 3D points using Morton codes—a spatial sorting method that naturally clusters similar points together. Each feature is split into a precise main part (called a base) and a small remainder (called an offset) that only needs low precision since it's numerically small. The system applies two levels of precision reduction: first shrinking the remainders to low precision, then tuning the precision format for each region based on the actual patterns in that region's remainders. The hardware and algorithm are designed together so the Morton code sorting and main computation can run in parallel, avoiding bottlenecks.
key_novelty: The core idea is applying spatial grouping via Morton codes, then using region-aware precision reduction that adapts to each region's actual feature patterns.
contributions: Morton-code-based spatial locality capture enabling region-level feature decomposition into base and offset components
Two-level mixed-precision quantization: base kept high-precision while offsets use low-precision, with region-adaptive dual-precision at level two
Hardware architecture co-design parallelizing Morton code computation with critical execution path
Demonstrates 12X speedup over CPU and 2.8-3.8X over state-of-the-art ASICs with negligible accuracy degradation
limitations: Scalability to very large point clouds and applicability to non-point-cloud 3D representations not discussed.
primary_theme: Spatial locality-aware mixed-precision quantization for point cloud acceleration
